LESSON: ACIDS, BASES AND INDICATORS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: INTEGRAT ED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements and Compounds
Topic 2.2: Acids, bases and indicators
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 22

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Acids, bases and indicators, part of Mixtures, Elements and Compounds in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven INTEGRAT ED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why are acids and bases important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify acids and bases using a litmus paper,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Acids, bases and indicators in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. prepare an acid-base indicator from plant extracts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Acids, bases and indicators in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe the physical properties of acids and bases,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Acids, bases and indicators in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. outline applications of acids, bases and indicators in real life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Acids, bases and indicators in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the uses of acids and bases in real life. ● Learners are guided on how to use litmus paper to classify household solutions into acids and bases. Learners with blindness are given verbal description on colour change on the litmus paper in presence of an acid or a base. ● In pairs, learners are guided to crush parts of a plant such as petals of a flower to prepare plant extract indicators using locally available materials and dispose laboratory waste responsibly. Learners with blindness are given verbal descriptions of the colour of the plant extract indicator. ● Learners are guided to use plant extract indicators to classify common household solutions such as soap solution, Why are acids and bases important? 16 ● uses of acids, bases and indicators in real life wood ash solution, toothpaste, lemon juice, sour milk, tap water as either acidic, neutral or basic. Learners with low vision are guided to identify the colour change of the indicator while learners with blindness are given verbal descriptions on the colour change of the indicator. Where possible learners with blindness use a talking colour detector device to note the colour change. ● Learners are guided to carry out activities to investigate physical properties of acids and bases. Learners with blindness are given verbal descriptions of the colour change during the activity. ● Learners are guided to use digital devices with assistive technology, print or braille media to explore applications of acids and bases. 17 Precaution: Observe cyber security measures when using digital devices.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Acids, bases and indicators together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: The learner acquires data recording and presentation techniques as carry out activities to

investigate the physical properties of acids and bases.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner develops research skills as they explore applications of acids and bases using

print or digital media.

● Creativity and Imagination: The learner acquires innovative practices as they use acid-base indicator from plant extracts to

classify common household solutions as either acidic or basic.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner engages in assigned roles as they carry out activities to prepare acid-base indicators from plant

extracts collaboratively.

● Respect: The learner appreciates diverse opinions of peers as they collaboratively use digital or print or braille media to explore

applications of acids and bases and present findings in plenary.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio-economic and Environmental issues: The learner observes cyber security measures while using digital media to explore

applications of acids and bases.
